components.name: Square-basin rough-window recursion and high least-factor contraction
components.project_addition: Apply established rough-number and Buchstab least-factor recursion to the exact finite cofactor windows forced by consecutive-square geometry; combine the square-derived raw window width with quotient-response transport to prove a high least-factor contraction threshold p^2>=2k, binary second-factor branches, pairwise cofactor-support separation, finite three-prime resource bounds, exact identification of child branch bits with earlier square-basin hit counts H_(p*ell)(k), multiplicative capacity from non-reuse of prime resources, basin-level cross-shell hit-state unions, and exact finite hit-count envelopes for both the full high-band composite population and the three-prime subset. The square-derived prime intervals then yield classical-analytic density ceilings log(2) for all high-band composites and log(2)/2 for high-band three-prime states after applying established reciprocal-prime and prime-counting estimates.
